questions.q: Auto parks the robot turned 45°. TeleOp starts and field-centric uses the IMU. What happens when the driver pushes the stick straight up?
questions.correct: It drives off about 45° to the side
wrong: It drives straight away from the drivers
It waits until auto runs one more time
It spins in place until the driver lets go
questions.explain: The IMU calls 'forward' whichever way the robot faced when TeleOp started. If that's 45° off, every stick push comes out 45° off.

questions.correct: Storage in the FTC software that lasts between OpModes
wrong: A whiteboard the drive team uses to write the plan
A file the Driver Hub saves between two matches
The Pinpoint's own memory chip for positions
questions.explain: blackboard is shared storage that lives across OpMode runs (but not across a robot restart), so auto can leave a note for TeleOp.

questions.q: Why does auto write its position to the blackboard every loop, instead of only at the end?
questions.correct: The 30-second timer can cut auto off mid-path
wrong: Writing it only once would take far too long
The blackboard erases itself after every second
TeleOp reads it 50 times a second during auto
questions.explain: If auto is cut off mid-path, the last note written is still the robot's real position.

questions.q: Why does TeleOp use blackboard.remove("autoPose") instead of just reading it?
questions.correct: It uses the note up, so an old one is never trusted
wrong: Because remove() runs faster than plain get()
The blackboard only lets you read a note once
It deletes the auto program so it can't rerun
questions.explain: remove() reads the note and throws it away. Restart TeleOp later in practice and it won't trust a position from a robot that may have been carried somewhere else.

questions.q: Why does TeleOp wait until after START to call setPose()?
questions.correct: The Pinpoint is still calibrating, and could erase it
wrong: The rules don't allow setPose() during INIT
The blackboard stays empty until START is pressed
The robot has to drive forward a little first
questions.explain: The Pinpoint takes a moment to calibrate after its INIT reset. Sending the pose after START makes sure it sticks.

questions.q: TeleOp starts with no note on the blackboard. What does isPoseKnown() return?
wrong: true
The last position from auto
questions.explain: poseKnown starts false and only turns true when setPose() runs: from auto's note or from a HOME reset. No note means we don't guess.

questions.q: Which three things pin down HOME, so the robot can be placed there without measuring?
questions.correct: Back on your wall, facing away, left side on the tape
wrong: Field center, facing the hive, touching nothing
Any corner at all, touching two walls at once
Wherever auto happened to park the robot last
questions.explain: The wall fixes y, facing straight away fixes the heading (90°), and the tape line fixes x.

questions.q: Why is HOME at x = -13 and not x = -22, the tape line?
questions.correct: The pose is the robot's center: add half its width
wrong: Because -13 is closer to the hive than -22
Because the tape line is 9 inches wide
Because the Pinpoint can't read below -20
questions.explain: TAPE_X + ROBOT_WIDTH / 2 = -22 + 9 = -13. The same idea gives HOME_Y = -71 + 9 = -62.

questions.q: Why do you HOLD RB for half a second at HOME instead of tapping it?
questions.correct: So a bumped button can't scramble its position
wrong: The IMU needs half a second to spin up first
A quick tap of RB is reserved for the intake
The Driver Hub ignores any short button press
questions.explain: The ElapsedTime stopwatch restarts every loop RB is up. Only a deliberate half-second hold triggers the reset.

questions.q: What happens if a driver holds RB somewhere that is NOT HOME?
questions.correct: It believes it's at HOME, so its position is now wrong
wrong: Nothing: the robot checks it's really at HOME
The robot drives itself straight back to HOME
The robot stops completely until the match ends
questions.explain: The robot can't check. A HOME reset says 'you are exactly here', so only press it at HOME.

questions.q: Once the pose is known, field-centric uses which heading?
wrong: The IMU heading, plus 90° to match
Always 0°, so it drives robot-centric
The heading the auto started out with
questions.explain: The Pinpoint knows the true field heading. Facing away from your drivers is field heading 90°, and field-centric calls that 0, so subtract 90.

questions.q: The robot faces straight away from your drivers. Its field heading is 90°. What heading does field-centric get?
questions.explain: 90 - 90 = 0: 'straight ahead' for the driver. That's exactly what the IMU reads at HOME after resetYaw(), so the two agree.

questions.q: What does the Driver Hub's TeleOp preselect do when auto ends?
questions.correct: Selects your TeleOp; drivers still press INIT and START
wrong: Starts your TeleOp running all by itself
Runs INIT on your TeleOp automatically
Restarts the auto from the very beginning
questions.explain: For safety it only queues the TeleOp. The drivers still press INIT, then START.

questions.q: A driver presses STOP in the middle of auto. What happens to the TeleOp preselect?
questions.correct: It's cancelled: no switch to the TeleOp
wrong: It switches to the TeleOp right away
It starts the TeleOp running immediately
It waits 30 seconds, then switches anyway
questions.explain: The switch only happens when auto ends on its own or is stopped by the 30-second timer, not when a person presses STOP.
